**TL;DR** — Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5 on July 24 as its new flagship for long-running agents and coding, while a critical unauthenticated RCE bug in Gitea (CVE-2026-59774, CVSS 9.8) is the thing every self-hoster should patch today.

## Anthropic and Claude
- **Claude Opus 5** released July 24 — new flagship for the Opus tier, pitched as a step change for long-running agents, coding, and professional work; same pricing as Opus 4.8 ($5/$25 per M tokens), reportedly beats Opus 4.8 on SWE-bench Verified and Frontier-Bench v0.1. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news)
- **Claude Code** shipped near-daily point releases all week (2.1.221→2.1.231, Aug 4–13): notable ones are self-hosted runner support (`claude self-hosted-runner`, 2.1.224), a new Focus view (`Ctrl+Alt+F`, 2.1.221), and a run of security fixes closing permission-check bypasses, worktree-isolation bypasses, and sandbox escapes (2.1.221–2.1.223). [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- **AI-content watermarking** — Anthropic posted on how Claude marks AI-generated text, aimed at EU AI Act compliance; technical details on the watermarking method are still thin. (via Daring Fireball, linking out) [Daring Fireball](https://daringfireball.net/)
- Leadership: Mariano-Florentino Cuéllar joined as Chief Global Affairs Officer (Aug 4); Anthropic also published a position on open-weights models and expanded its Cognizant enterprise partnership (Jul 27). [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news)

## NixOS ecosystem
- **The Nixpkgs Core Team disbanded**, announced Aug 7 by Alyssa Ross — the team was down to two people at the end; the post drew 30k+ views within a day, so expect governance/PR-review changes to ripple through nixpkgs contribution flow. Outside the approved list (NixOS Discourse), flagging explicitly. [NixOS Discourse](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/the-nixpkgs-core-team-has-disbanded/79413)
- **Documentation team funding push** (Jul 10, still the most recent post on the official blog) — volunteers seeking financial support to improve onboarding docs. (ongoing) [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/)
- Nothing newer on the official NixOS Blog itself this week — last dated post is the July 10 documentation-funding note; NixOS 26.05 ("unnamed yet") remains the current stable release from May 30. (ongoing) [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/)

## AI coding agents and agent frameworks
- **Meta launched Muse Code** (~Aug 5), a terminal-based coding agent built on the new Muse Spark 1.2 model, aimed at large-repo software engineering with multi-subagent orchestration — Meta's first real swing at the Claude Code/Codex space. Outside approved list (via Daring Fireball link-out + TechCrunch). [Daring Fireball](https://daringfireball.net/)
- **Claude Code** remains the fastest-moving agent CLI this week by release cadence — see changelog details above, notably self-hosted runners and cross-session messaging. [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- No major new agent-framework paper or eval (LangGraph/CrewAI-class) surfaced in the approved sources this week; general web search mostly turned up SEO listicles, which I'm not treating as signal.

## Self-hosting and homelab
- **Critical Gitea vulnerability, CVE-2026-59774 / GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r (CVSS 9.8)** — unauthenticated attacker can abuse Org-mode markup rendering (`#+INCLUDE`) on any public repo to read arbitrary files, chainable to RCE via `INTERNAL_TOKEN` extraction and a malicious Git hook. Affects 1.22.1–1.27.0, fixed in 1.27.1 — patch immediately if your instance has any public repo reachable from the internet. Outside approved list (official GitHub advisory). [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/security/advisories/GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r)
- Claude Code's new **self-hosted runner** support (`claude self-hosted-runner`, 2.1.224) is directly relevant if you're running agent CI on your own homelab hardware. [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)

## Local and on-device LLM inference
- **Meta released Muse Glimmer**, a 30B-parameter open-weight agentic model (Apache 2.0, Aug 10) built via distillation from Muse Spark, designed to run entirely on a single consumer GPU for always-on local agent workflows; available now on Hugging Face, with Ollama/LM Studio/Unsloth support "coming soon." Outside approved list (Meta AI Research). [Meta AI Research](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-glimmer-open-agentic-model)
- **llama.cpp** (ongoing, week of Aug 4–11): added NVFP4 quantization support to `llama-quantize`, BailingMoE/Ling 3.0 flash support with speculative decoding, and Qwen3-TTS speech synthesis — audio is becoming a first-class citizen alongside text/vision. Outside approved list. [Buttondown weekly report](https://buttondown.com/weekly-project-news/archive/weekly-github-report-for-llamacpp-august-04-2026-6176/)
